# Copilot / AI Agent Instructions

This Unity project contains gameplay code, generated SRP command-buffer wrappers, and a custom IK system. The goal of this file is to give an AI coding agent concise, actionable context so it can be productive immediately.

1) Big-picture architecture
- Unity project root with Editor-managed assemblies (open with Unity Editor). See ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt for editor version.
- Gameplay: `Assets/StarterAssets/ThirdPersonController` contains player movement (see `ThirdPersonController.cs`) — handles input via an `IInputProvider` abstraction, animator usage via `TryGetComponent(out Animator)`, and a vaulting subsystem guarded by `DebugVault` flags and editor gizmos.
- Custom IK: `Assets/HomebrewIK` holds the project's IK implementation (treat as a subsystem; prefer small, non-invasive changes unless requested).
- Rendering wrappers: top-level files like `ComputeCommandBuffer.cs`, `UnsafeCommandBuffer.cs`, `RasterCommandBuffer.cs` are auto-generated command-buffer wrappers (do NOT modify directly — they are generated from Unity SRP reflection).

2) Where to read first (key examples)
- Player input + movement: `Assets/StarterAssets/ThirdPersonController/Scripts/ThirdPersonController.cs` (vault intent checks, `HasVaultMovementIntent()`, `TryGetVaultLanding()` and `PerformVault()` coroutine).
- Input binding asset: `Assets/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions` (project uses the new Input System when `ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` is defined).
- Command buffer generator hints: interfaces at repo root (`IComputeCommandBuffer.cs`, `IUnsafeCommandBuffer.cs`, `IBaseCommandBuffer.cs`) and generated wrappers (root .cs files) — these are generated by SRP tooling.

3) Project-specific patterns and conventions
- Inspector-first configuration: public fields use `[Header]`, `[Tooltip]`, ranges and inspector-friendly defaults — change inspector values via Unity Editor, not hardcode values in scripts.
- Input abstraction: code depends on `IInputProvider`. Look for implementations like `StarterAssetsInputs` or `EnemyInputAI` rather than coupling to `PlayerInput` directly.
- Compile-time features: code uses `#if ENABLE_INPUT_SYSTEM` to support both input systems — be careful when editing input-related code to preserve both paths.
- Generated code: large command-buffer files at repo root are generated — if you need to change command buffer behavior, update generator in the SRP package (not these files) or adjust calling code.
- Debugging toggles: many subsystems expose boolean debug flags (e.g., `DebugVault`, `DebugVaultGizmos`) and use `Debug.Log` — useful for small runtime investigations.

4) Build / run / debug workflows
- Primary: open the project in the Unity Editor (use the version in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`). Use the Editor Play mode for gameplay/physics/animation debugging.
- Code edit loop: edit scripts in the `Assets/` folder, switch back to the Editor to compile and run. For C# project-level editing, open `ThirdPersonIK_Controller.sln` in Visual Studio or Rider.
- Native/Render pipeline code: generated command buffer files are part of a render-pipeline workflow. Do not run `dotnet build` expecting a Unity build; use Unity Editor or the Editor's build pipeline.
- Attaching debugger: attach Visual Studio / Rider to Unity Editor process for live debugging and breakpoints.

5) When to change generated files
- NEVER edit `ComputeCommandBuffer.cs`, `UnsafeCommandBuffer.cs`, `RasterCommandBuffer.cs` directly. Instead:
  - If a new CommandBuffer API must be exposed, update the generator (this project does not include the SRP generator — it lives in `com.unity.render-pipelines.core` package). Note this is an advanced change.

6) Good-first tasks for AI agents
- Small gameplay fixes or refactors inside `Assets/StarterAssets` (preserve inspector-exposed APIs). Example: tune vault thresholds in `ThirdPersonController.cs` or extract vault checks into a helper class.
- Add additional `IInputProvider` implementations for non-player agents (follow the `IInputProvider` lookup pattern in `Start()` of `ThirdPersonController`).

7) Useful file pointers
- Player controller: Assets/StarterAssets/ThirdPersonController/Scripts/ThirdPersonController.cs
- Input asset: Assets/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions
- Custom IK: Assets/HomebrewIK/
- Generated render wrappers: ComputeCommandBuffer.cs, UnsafeCommandBuffer.cs, RasterCommandBuffer.cs (top-level)
- Solutions: ThirdPersonIK_Controller.sln, ThirdPersonIk.sln

If anything is unclear or you want the document to emphasize other areas (build automation, tests, or a deeper walkthrough of `HomebrewIK`), tell me which area to expand. I'll iterate quickly.
